original_text: U.S. retail and food services sales increased more than expected in March 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, as the war with Iran pushed gasoline prices sharply higher and produced a record increase in nominal receipts at gasoline stations, while larger tax refunds likely supported spending in other categories. Because the retail sales figures are adjusted for inflation, higher prices accounted for only a small part of the strongest monthly increase in a year. Nevertheless, relatively solid underlying sales prompted some economists to raise their estimates for first-quarter economic growth to at least 5.5%.
